approved_by_me.description: true: your latest review must approve it, a person's pull request too, unlike the built-in "approved by me"; false: none of yours does.

authors.description: The logins the author must be one of; bots without app/.

bot.description: true: the author must be a bot; false: a person.

checks.description: The states its checks must be in one of: "passing" (passed, none at all, or only checks.approval pending), "failing" or "pending" (still running).

created_before_days.description: The least days, of 24 hours, since it was created.

created_within_days.description: The most days, of 24 hours, since it was created.

decision.description: The review decisions REVIEW shows, one of which it must have; "none" is none, as in a repository that requires no review.

draft.description: true: it must be a draft, which S never selects, so [[select]] does not take true; false: ready for review.

dry_run.description: true: only tell, in the notifications, what the rule would approve.

labels.description: Labels one of which it must have.

max_files.description: The most files it may change.

max_lines.description: The most lines it may add and delete together: the sum of the two numbers SIZE shows.

merge.description: Whether GitHub would let it be merged now, one of: "ready" (the merge button can be pressed), "behind" (its branch must be brought up to date), "conflict" (it conflicts with its base), "blocked" (its reviews or required checks hold it, or it is a draft) or "unknown" (GitHub is still working it out).

min_files.description: The least files it may change.

min_lines.description: The least lines it may add and delete together.

mine.description: true: it must be your own pull request; false: someone else's.

name.description: The rule's name, which the notifications say of what it approved; without one, they say the rule's conditions.

packages.description: The dependencies a renovate or dependabot pull request updates, read from its body; every one it updates must be listed.

query.description: The GitHub search the pull requests are found by; without it, the open pull requests that are not drafts and whose review is asked of you, in the rule's repos when each can be searched. A rule with neither query nor a condition is a mistake.

reasons.description: Reasons of a notification, one of which the row's must have; S and a rule that approves judge a pull request without one, so [[select]] and [[auto_approve]] do not take it.

repos.description: owner/repo globs the repository must match one of; * matches any part of the owner or the name.

requested.description: Whom a review must be asked of, one of them: "me", a team as "@slug", or "@*" for any team.

reviewed_by_me.description: true: you must have reviewed it, whatever the review said; false: you have not.

state.description: The states it must be in one of: "open", "merged" or "closed"; S selects open ones only, so [[select]] takes "open" alone.

title.description: A regular expression the title must match, as written: a shortcode such as `:arrow_up:` is matched as itself, not as its emoji. An empty one sets no condition.

updated_before_days.description: The least days, of 24 hours, since it was last updated, as AGE counts them in a search tab.

updated_within_days.description: The most days, of 24 hours, since it was last updated: a label or a bot's comment updates it too. An old pull request updated lately matches.

attention_paths.description: Pull requests changing files that match these glob patterns get a mark in the confirm popup, which names the patterns matched; a pattern of one file is named by the file name, as CODEOWNERS.

dir.description: Where gh-desk keeps its clones and the worktrees Claude reads, and the lists last read (lists.json, shown at once at the next launch) (~ is your home); by default $XDG_CACHE_HOME/gh-desk, or ~/.cache/gh-desk.

approval.description: Checks that pass only after an approval, such as a policy bot's: glob patterns of check names. While only they are pending, CI shows ◌, and the checks count as passing when deciding a merge.

wait_timeout.description: How long a merge, or an approval asked to wait, waits for the jobs still at work on the pull request's head, required or not; an admin merge also waits for the required checks within it. Only the time gh-desk is running counts.

claude.description: C and i ask Claude Code (claude -p, with the account you are signed in with). i, or ask claude about it in the menu of enter, reviews the pull request under the cursor in a worktree of its head. C plans what to show and select in the tab shown, with no tools, and answers in the language you ask in; enter applies the plan, and an approve or a merge in it opens the confirm popup. Claude's own tools only read: no settings files are loaded, its file tools see only the worktree and the skills of plugins, and it has none that run commands. The conversation also takes the MCP servers of [claude.mcp] and the skills of plugins, which can do whatever they are made to.

allowed_tools.description: The tools Claude may use, among "Read", "Grep", "Glob" and "WebFetch".

command.description: The claude command: a name looked up on PATH, or a path to it (~ is your home), without arguments.

instructions.description: Appended to the instructions of every review and triage, such as "Point out changes that have no tests."

language.description: The language Claude answers in about a pull request, such as "Japanese". A review drafted with D is written in the language of the pull request instead.

mcp.description: The MCP servers of the conversation about a pull request: gh-desk's own, and yours.

builtin.description: Give the conversation gh-desk's own MCP server, whose tools read the pull request's repository and nothing else: its checks and CI logs, its issues and pull requests. They only read, without a prompt, what anyone who sees the pull request can see. Left out, it is on, unless allowed_tools has WebFetch or servers has one: either could send what the tools read out of the conversation, so then write true or false.

servers.description: Your MCP servers for the conversation about a pull request, by name, written as Claude Code configures a server (command, args, env; or type, url, headers), with tools: the server's tools that may run without a prompt. A server started with a command runs in the cache, not in the worktree. ${GH_DESK_OWNER}, ${GH_DESK_REPO}, ${GH_DESK_NUMBER} and ${GH_DESK_URL} (the repository's URL) are the pull request; pass secrets as ${VAR} from your environment. What the pull request says may call these tools: a server that reads private data, together with WebFetch, lets it send the data out.

model.description: The model Claude Code runs, as claude --model takes it.

plugins.description: Plugins whose skills the conversation about a pull request takes, as their directories (~ is your home). Only the skills are taken, copied when gh-desk starts, as gh-desk:<name>; the rest of a plugin (hooks, MCP servers, language servers, commands) is not. A skill whose allowed-tools grants a tool outside allowed_tools, Skill and the tools of the MCP servers is a mistake.

release_notes_check.description: Let Claude read the release notes of the bot pull requests in the merge popup, and mark those that need care.

style.description: How a description and its comments are drawn in the pane: "rendered" (default) draws headings, lists, code, quotes and tables; "plain" shows the Markdown as written.

collapse.description: Files shown folded, as their name and line counts, until unfolded: glob patterns, matched against the base name unless they have a slash.

keys.description: Which keys do what, by action: a key or a list of keys, or [] to turn it off.

bell.description: Ring the terminal's bell when a reading of the inbox finds a notification newly unread: new, read before, or updated since. The first reading after start does not ring it, nor one of the excluded. The terminal rings, flashes or stays quiet as it is set to.

columns.description: The columns shown, in the order given; "pr" and "title" are needed. WHY shows when a row has something in it (whom a review is asked of, the reason of a notification), and AUTHOR not on a tab of your own pull requests. On a narrow terminal columns go before TITLE gets narrow: SIZE first, then AUTHOR, MERGE, WHY, AGE, REVIEW and CI.

home_owners.description: Owners whose name is left out of the PR column, such as your company.

refresh.description: Refresh every tab this often, as a Go duration such as "3m" or "90s"; "off" refreshes only when r is pressed.

scope.description: Narrow every tab to one owner, repository ("repo") or author at a time, chosen on the header with < and >, or from a list with O; left out, the tabs are not narrowed. The one chosen is kept for the next launch.

stale_days.description: Mark AGE when a pull request has not been updated for this many days, or "off".

level.description: How much goes to the log file: "debug", "info" (default), "warn" or "error". --debug and GH_DESK_LOG_LEVEL take precedence. gh desk log prints where the file is.

actions.description: The actions the menu of enter offers, in the order given. One left out is not in the menu; its key still runs it from the list.

auto_merge.description: Use GitHub's auto-merge where the repository allows it; elsewhere gh-desk waits for the checks and merges when they pass. Commits pushed after auto-merge is turned on are merged too, as GitHub does.

blocked_timeout.description: Where gh-desk waits, how long a pull request may stay blocked by another rule (a second approval, code owners) after its jobs finished. Only the time gh-desk is running counts.

methods.description: The order of preference among the methods a repository allows: "merge", "squash", "rebase". The first one the repository allows is used.

update_branch.description: Whose branch is updated when it is behind its base: "humans" (default), "all" or "never". Bots rebase their own branches, and some (renovate) stop updating a branch someone else committed to.

height.description: Lines of the preview pane under the list; 0 hides it until it is shown with a key. Dragging the pane's top edge, or + and -, changes them, and the lines set that way are kept over this one.

tab.description: The tab the pane opens on: "overview" (default), the description beside a column of facts, or "diff".

check.description: Read gh-desk's releases on GitHub once a day, and tell in the notifications of a newer release and, after an update, of the update. Only the builds of a release read them; GH_NO_EXTENSION_UPDATE_NOTIFIER turns it off too.

editor.description: The editor ctrl+e opens to write a review, with its arguments, such as "code --wait". Left out, $VISUAL, then $EDITOR.

mark_done.description: Mark a pull request's notification done after you review it here, from any tab.

sections.description: The parts a tab's rows are split into, in the order shown, each an inline table: a name (its head; without one, no head), show ("open", "folded" or "excluded") and the conditions of a rule. A section whose conditions wait for what is not read yet is passed over, and never leaves a row out.

dark.description: The color scheme on a dark terminal, and on one that does not tell its background.

light.description: The color scheme on a light terminal. Write the same theme as theme.dark to use it on any terminal.

shimmer.description: Run a light over the text that says what is going on, such as refreshing… or thinking…; the screen is drawn more often while something is read.

spinner.description: The spinner shown while something is read: "dots" (default) ⠋⠙⠹, "dense" ⣾⣽⣻, "bounce" ⠁⠂⠄, "snake" ⠉⠙⠚, "jump" ⢄⢂⢁, "fill" ⣀⣤⣶, "sand" ⡀⣀⣤, "line" |/-\, "arc" ◜◠◝, "quarter" ◴◷◶, "block" ▖▘▝, "star" ✶✸✹, or "off", a ⋯ that does not move and is left out before a line that says what is going on. The progress pane of the log viewer turns a spinner and marks of its own, which "off" stops too.
